summary: mžd and yžd duplicate the same verb and several attestations
rationale: The supplied lookup for yžd gives the same MEA yšṭ (Af.) etymology and meaning ausstrecken. Both entries quote the Emir extending his letter at 36/57, the imperative variants mžad; možád; ožád (665), and the infinitives mžodo (664) and tawžido (665). They divide the same material between stem I under mžd and stem III under yžd. Consolidate the duplicate analyses while preserving unique examples; the canonical root choice remains editorial.

summary: The current glossary assigns reduced mžəd-/možad- to mžd I even though its etymology overlaps yžd III. This run follows that established filing, explicitly marking the overlap instead of normalizing stems from historical expectations.

Active mžədle ruḥe has an explicit reflexive object; Detransitive mžīd has an affected subject without that object; Part. Pass. mžido predicates a resulting or static posture. These constructions do not require an external stretcher.
Infectum-wa gməždiwa adds habitual construction procedure with an inanimate beam object. Ordinary l-/laf-/ʕal- directions and m-marked wall/path do not establish extra senses.
The inherited bare root note 'n' and unglossed tawžido are left untouched; the latter is not a newly attested form in these occurrences.

Round 2, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations below reproduce the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses and sense distinctions rest on the Turoyo. Round-one proposals are retained as the comparison baseline and are not republished in this JSON.
Both tokens are active I Infectum with overt possessed body-part patients. They are not Detransitive, and the inherited mžd/yžd overlap is not a reason to change stem assignment here.
The existing Infectum I.1 cell is full after round one. The selected material appears only under Idiomatic phrases, without duplicate box examples.

Lookup searches for leg/tongue wording and entry yžd found physical extension but no matching figurative pair. The single paired occurrence supports provisional phrase indexing, not a claim of independent frequency or a proven contact origin.
Are mžd I and yžd III alternative analyses of one paradigm, or a synchronic contrast? A speaker paradigm is needed before merging the duplicate entry.
At MAC TERTO ZARE/61, confirm whether Komažḏo bəṯre is an established pursuit construction and whether it belongs to mžd I or yžd III; preserve žḏ as supplied.
Is Gmožadna at MAC Murder /89 merely a literal gesture plus metaphor, or a conventional authority expression? Confirm -na contraction and contact interpretation.
Check contracted məžde at 61/137 and feminine mžədto at 92/30 against listed mžido/mžītto. No silent vowel correction is made.
Confirm the Preterit reading of expanded možadla at 61/93; preserve the transmitted form.
Are the leg and tongue expressions conventional Turoyo collocations or locally created metaphors in this sermon? Each is attested here only once.
Do speakers associate the pair with a specific contact-language phrase? No contact source is asserted.

Crossbeam spanning retains physical extension with an inanimate object. Repeated Gmožadna in the boundary-setting dialogue carries a defiant reach/authority metaphor after Kurdish speech; this does not by itself prove a conventional idiom.
